parts.text: Give three reasons that SARS-CoV-2 has evolved into a worldwide pandemic and MERS-CoV did not.

questions.model_answer: 3 reasons SARS-CoV-2 caused a pandemic while MERS-CoV did not: (1) SARS-CoV-2 achieves substantial transmission from pre-symptomatic and asymptomatic/mildly symptomatic individuals, allowing silent widespread community spread, whereas MERS-CoV transmission occurred predominantly from symptomatic, often severely ill patients, making case identification and containment easier; (2) SARS-CoV-2 binds ACE2 receptors that are abundant in the upper respiratory tract, favoring efficient respiratory droplet/aerosol transmission between casual contacts, whereas MERS-CoV's DPP4 receptor is more predominant in the lower respiratory tract, requiring closer/prolonged contact for transmission and resulting in lower overall transmissibility (lower R0); (3) MERS-CoV had a geographically limited zoonotic reservoir and exposure route (dromedary camels concentrated in the Arabian Peninsula), limiting global spread, whereas SARS-CoV-2 spread efficiently and rapidly worldwide via international travel before containment measures could be implemented.

parts.text: MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 are both coronaviruses. What are 3 reasons that aren’t social or pandemic management for why SARS-CoV-2 is so different, i.e why it caused a pandemic?

questions.model_answer: Three virologic/biologic (non-social) features favoring SARS-CoV-2's pandemic spread over MERS-CoV: (1) Efficient replication in the upper respiratory tract/nasopharynx (high ACE2 receptor expression there), enabling substantial presymptomatic and asymptomatic transmission via respiratory droplets, whereas MERS-CoV (using DPP4) replicates predominantly in the lower respiratory tract and required close/prolonged contact for transmission. (2) A higher basic reproduction number (R0) reflecting more efficient human-to-human transmissibility. (3) A furin cleavage site in the spike protein that enhances cell entry/fusion efficiency and broadens tissue tropism, facilitating more efficient transmission compared with MERS-CoV.

questions.question: Aside from public health measures and isolation, what three differences make SARS-CoV worse than MERS?

parts.text: Aside from public health measures and isolation, what three differences make SARS-CoV worse than MERS?

cohort_answer.text: Higher R0 (MERS <1, COVID-19 ~3, SARS ~1.5); more asymptomatic spread; less virulent.
